title: Severance
synopsis: The doors close. The procedure begins. Who do you become when the floor ticks down?

nodes.text: Lumon's hush. Milchick's smile. The elevator opens. Floor 4 comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Step in” and “Slip a note into your own pocket.” In Lobby, 8:47, even a sensible delay gives the threat another way in.

choices.consequence: You choose to step in. By Floor 4, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Slip a note into your own pocket
choices.consequence: You commit to slip a note into your own pocket. It carries you into Floor 4 while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Threshold flickers. You are at your desk, refining numbers you don't remember asking for. Mark will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Refine the scary cluster” than after “Hide them in a folder.”

choices.consequence: You commit to refine the scary cluster. It carries you into Mark while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You hide them in a folder. The way toward Mark opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: End of shift. The doors close. Whoever you've been today, dissolves. The paths divide here: “Believe you'll come back” leads into Break the Floor, while “Hope your other self does too” makes Pay Day, Forever the next reckoning. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Above Ground in play.

choices.consequence: You commit to believe you'll come back. It carries you into Break the Floor while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Hope your other self does too
choices.consequence: You commit to hope your other self does too. It carries you into Pay Day, Forever while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You commit to take the third path. It carries you into Above Ground while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The recording leaks. The hearings begin. Floor 4 is dismantled, gently, over months. You meet your outie in a coffee shop and don't know what to say. The road into Break the Floor began with “Believe you'll come back” in Elevator Down; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You step into the lobby with no memory of the day. Soup on the way home. The soup is good. The soup is, you tell yourself, good. The road into Pay Day, Forever began with “Hope your other self does too” in Elevator Down; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You make it out before Lumon catches up. A man on a loading dock says, simply, 'You're early.' He does not, you realize, mean today. The road into Above Ground began with “Take the third path” in Elevator Down; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
